title: Oncall handoff + temp runbook (night shift)
content:
Shift: 03/01 20:00 PST -> 03/02 08:00 PST
Primary focus: keep inference runtime healthy, watch for latency regressions, and handle any GPU node failures or model OOMs. This is a working handoff doc	 add notes to bottom during your shift.

Summary of state at start:
- Production serving-runtime stable but slightly elevated p95 token latency (~820ms) for short-chat routes. Baseline usually ~700ms. No errors above normal rate.
- One dedicated GPU node (gpu-prod-5) reported transient NVIDIA driver disconnects earlier; automated restart succeeded. File ticket SRE-3421 for follow-up.
- Redis KV-cache eviction spikes at ~10:30 UTC yesterday due to cold-start of a few large models; cache hit ratio ~82% (target 90%).

Things to watch (alerts + dashboards):
- PagerDuty alert names to watch:
  - SRE: Serving-runtime-high-error-rate
  - SRE: Serving-runtime-high-latency
  - SRE: GPU-node-down
  - SRE: KV-cache-evictions-high
- Dashboards: Console -> Models > Per-route p50/p95/p99, infra -> GPU utilization (per-node), redis -> key eviction rate, kinesis/kafka consumer lag for batchers.
- Slack: #sre-oncall for incident coordination, #infra-ops for infra changes. Phone escalation (L2): Jordan Lee (@jordan-lee) if PD escalation fails.

Quick checks on takeover:
1) Basic health
   - curl -s https://status.redwood.ai/api/health | jq .  (expect ok)
   - kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | egrep "CrashLoopBackOff|Evicted"
2) Latency and errors
   - grafana: inference/requests -> check p95 for "chat-short" and "generation-long" routes last 1h vs 24h.
   - kibana: query "level:ERROR AND (serving-runtime)" timeframe last 1h.
3) GPU nodes
   - kubectl get nodes -l node-role.kubernetes.io/gpu=true -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,STATUS:.status.conditions[-1].type,READY:.status.conditions[?(@.type==\"Ready\")].status
   - If node NotReady or kubelet restarting: check node logs via journalctl -u kubelet on the host (requires bastion access). If driver disconnects, try safe restart: systemctl restart nvidia-driver || reboot node (prefer restart first). Notify infra channel before reboot.
4) KV cache (redis)
   - redis-cli -h redis-cache.prod info stats | egrep "evicted_keys|keyspace_hits|keyspace_misses"
   - If evicted_keys spike: increase cache-memory temporarily (only by infra on-call) OR restart the cache cluster rolling restart if a memory leak suspected. File follow-up ticket.

Temporary procedures / quick mitigations (use these if incident and we're under time pressure):
- High p95 latency for short-chat route with stable error rate:
  1) Check batcher backlog (kafka consumer lag). If huge lag, trigger consumer restart for the batcher group for the route: kafka-consumer-restart --group batcher-short-chat --topic incoming-requests
  2) If batcher healthy, consider dropping to a smaller model variant for the route (route controlled via model-router config): curl -X POST "$ROUTER_API/routes/chat-short/override" -d '{"model":"redwood-mini-v2-quant"}' and monitor latency. This is temporary	 revert after peak.
- GPU node OOM / model OOM during generation:
  1) If single pod OOMs repeatedly, scale down concurrency for that deployment: kubectl -n inference scale deployment/<deploy-name> --replicas=0; then inspect logs, restart with lower concurrency env var (MODEL_MAX_BATCH_TOKENS).
  2) If node OOM across pods, cordon node: kubectl cordon <node>, then drain with --ignore-daemonsets and restart node. Escalate to infra if hardware issue.
- Persistent redis evictions during peak:
  1) Add temporary TTL on large keys to reduce pressure (only if you understand key structure).
  2) Route heavy routes to model variant with smaller KV usage.

Common commands (copy-paste friendly):
- Check pods: kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide --sort-by=.status.startTime
- Check logs (stream): kubectl -n inference logs -f deployment/serving-runtime --tail=200
- Restart deployment safely: kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/model-router --timeout=10m

Unresolved items / ongoing follow-ups:
- SRE-3421: investigate gpu-prod-5 driver disconnects (owner: Jordan Lee)
- PERF-118: improve KV cache hotkey handling for large-models (owner: Applied ML)
- ACTION: Add alert runbook links into pagerduty alerts (owner: me/samira).

Notes to next oncall (please append):
- If you trigger model downgrade for short-chat route, put a note in the route-change log (confluence & #sre-oncall) and create a temporary rollback step.
- If you end up rebooting a GPU host, add the node id in this doc + time + reason.

During shift, add incidents here (timestamped):
- 2026-03-01T22:14Z - observed p95 spike to 1.2s for chat-short; downgraded to redwood-mini-v2-quant at 22:20Z. p95 back to ~730ms at 22:28Z. Logged to SRE-3422.

TODOs (short):
- move this to formal runbook page in Confluence with sanitized commands (owner: Samira)
- follow up with infra about driver flakiness (owner: Jordan)

References / useful links:
- Oncall runbook (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Oncall+Runbook
- Infra PR for autoscaler changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/512
- Ticket tracker: https://linear.app/redwood/label/sre

End of handoff.
